name: Bind a simple book
blurb: A pamphlet stitch is 20 minutes; a proper multi-signature case-bound notebook is a weekend and produces something genuinely beautiful.
gear: Paper, bookbinding thread and a needle
An awl, a bone folder, PVA glue
Bookcloth or card for the cover, and clamps
steps: Learn to fold signatures: sets of four or five sheets folded together, creased hard with a bone folder.
Learn the pamphlet stitch on a single signature as a first, complete project.
Learn to punch consistent sewing stations using a template so every signature aligns.
Learn the coptic or the French link stitch to join multiple signatures into a text block.
Glue and press the spine, then round it if you want, and add end papers.
Make a case from board and cloth, and case the text block in, pressing it flat overnight.
tips: Grain direction matters. Paper and board should have their grain running head to tail, or the book will warp.
Press everything, at every stage, for longer than feels necessary.
Use PVA rather than a hot glue gun, which goes brittle and fails within a year.
proof: A hand-bound notebook that opens flat, has a square spine, and survives being carried around.
